subject: business-studies
title: Break-Even: Where Revenue Catches Total Cost Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says total cost starts at zero like revenue. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - all cost lines start at zero

Fixed costs stay flat at $2,000 at every output, so total cost starts at the fixed-cost intercept and rises only by the $10 variable cost per unit; total revenue starts at zero and rises faster at the $20 selling price, so the two lines cross once, at the break-even output of 200 units.
Total cost starts at $4,000, because that is break-even revenue
Fixed costs rise with output, so total cost is curved

questions.misconception: Fixed costs rise as output rises, so total cost starts at zero like revenue.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: Fixed costs rise as output rises, so total cost starts at zero like revenue. Reteach point: Fixed costs stay flat at $2,000 at every output, so total cost starts at the fixed-cost intercept and rises only by the $10 variable cost per unit; total revenue starts at zero and rises faster at the $20 selling price, so the two lines cross once, at the break-even output of 200 units.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why there is a loss below 200 units.
questions.answer: Below 200 units total cost is above total revenue, because the $2,000 fixed costs have not yet been covered by contribution, so the business makes a loss.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names both lines: total cost above revenue below the crossing means loss.

questions.prompt: At 300 units, which statement is correct?

choices.text: Total revenue is $3,000 and total cost is $6,000, so there is a loss
Total revenue is $6,000 and total cost is $5,000, so there is a profit of $1,000
Total revenue and total cost are both $4,000, so it is break-even
Fixed costs have risen to $3,000 at 300 units

questions.feedback: At 300 units revenue is 300 times $20, which is $6,000, and total cost is $2,000 plus 300 times $10, which is $5,000.

questions.prompt: State the break-even output and break-even revenue, and show how you get them.
questions.answer: Break-even output is $2,000 fixed costs divided by $10 contribution per unit, which is 200 units; break-even revenue is 200 units times $20, which is $4,000.
questions.feedback: Credit the method: contribution first, then fixed costs divided by contribution, then check the crossing value of $4,000.
